slim.summary: The recall index is not yet safe to ship: it currently indexes conversation records that the authoritative convo fold would reject, and its rebuild hash does not cover all stored session fields.

findings.message: `refresh()` indexes raw `CONVO_OPENED` and `CONVO_TURN` records without applying the same fold rules as `ConvoStore`. A signed-but-invalid record that `cosmos_convo` would ignore (duplicate/malformed open, turn on a closed session, non-contiguous `seq`, etc.) still gets inserted into `sessions`/`turns` here and can later be returned by `search()`. That violates the stated 'projection, never authority' contract and can surface text that is not part of the authoritative conversation state.

`state_sha()` is supposed to prove rebuild parity, but the hash omits the `opened` column from the `sessions` table. If `refresh()` ever writes the wrong session-open timestamp, `rebuild()` will still report the same `state_sha`, so this drift check does not actually cover all persisted rows.
